Class Line

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.geometry.Line
public class Line extends Object
A three-dimensional parametric line, represented as p(t) = p0 + t * dp.

The same representation can be used as an infinite line or as a directed line segment. For an infinite line, t may be any real value. For the directed segment from p0 to p1, the segment corresponds to 0 <= t <= 1.

Author:
heddle

  • Constructor Details

    • Line

      public Line(Point po, Point p1)
      Creates a line from two points.

      If the line is interpreted as a directed segment, it runs from po to p1.

      Parameters:
      po - one point on the line
      p1 - another point on the line
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either point is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the two points are coincident, non-finite, or too close to define a stable direction

    • Line

      public Line(double[] p1, double[] p2)
      Creates a line from two arrays containing x, y, and z values.
      Parameters:
      p1 - one point as an xyz array
      p2 - another point as an xyz array
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if either array is null
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - if either array has fewer than three values
      IllegalArgumentException - if the two points are coincident or too close to define a stable direction

    • Line

      public Line(Line line)
      Creates a copy of another line.
      Parameters:
      line - the line to copy
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if line is null

    • Line

      public Line(Vector v)
      Creates a line through the origin in the direction of a vector.
      Parameters:
      v - the direction vector
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if v is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if v is the zero vector or too close to zero to define a stable direction

      public void getP(double t, Point p)
      Gets a point on the parametric line and stores it in an existing point.
      Parameters:

    • distance

      public double distance(Point p)
      Computes the shortest distance from this infinite line to a point.

      This method ignores segment endpoints. To use the finite segment distance, clamp the parameter returned by parameterOfClosestPoint(Point) to the interval [0, 1].

      Parameters:
      p - the point
      Returns:
      the perpendicular distance from p to the infinite line
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if p is null
